one_liner: Senior manager running FEMA's employee services office—federal retirement, benefits, employee relations, work-life and telework—supervising HR staff and advising agency leadership.
fit_summary: This GS-15 job requires a full year of GS-14-equivalent experience administering federal retirement and benefits programs (FEHB, FEGLI, FERS/CSRS, TSP), advising senior leaders on employee relations, and supervising HR staff. Nothing on file shows HR work for Daniel, and IEM emergency-management consulting does not substitute for it. Daniel's people skills and FEMA-adjacent background are real assets, but they don't meet these four required elements.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens), but you must show one year of specialized experience at GS-14 level that meets all four elements: retirement/benefits administration, employee relations advising, supervising HR staff, and HR process improvement.
No education can substitute for experience, so a degree will not qualify you.
You must pass and keep a Top Secret background investigation, which can include a credit check, and you must register with Selective Service if that applies to you.
You must be able to deploy anywhere in the U.S. and its territories on little notice, for weeks to months, and qualify for a government travel card.
This is a Schedule Policy/Career excepted-service job: it is at-will, with no MSPB appeal rights for adverse actions.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether any IEM work involved HR, benefits, or supervising staff; if not, skip this posting, because applying is unlikely to succeed.

Instead, target FEMA or DHS jobs that fit an IEM consulting background, such as Emergency Management Specialist (GS-0089), Program Analyst (GS-0343), or FEMA CORE/Reservist roles, at grades your actual experience supports.
Also look at external affairs, intergovernmental affairs, or congressional affairs roles at FEMA and Virginia VDEM, which use your policy knowledge and public-facing strengths.
If you do apply here, preview the USA Hire questionnaire at the link in the posting and answer truthfully; overstating HR expertise can be caught at the resume review or the interview.
Any federal resume must stay within two pages and list, for each job, the title, employer, MM/DD/YY dates, hours per week, and duties written in your own words.
The window is only 10/26–10/30/2026, so have the resume ready beforehand and set aside time for the USA Hire assessment.
resume_bullets: [Title], IEM, [MM/DD/YY–MM/DD/YY], [hours]/week: Advised [government client type] leaders on [emergency management/recovery program] policy and compliance, supporting [scope, e.g., # of jurisdictions or $ program size].
Coordinated with [#] stakeholders, including [federal/state/local officials], to resolve [type of complex issue], improving [process or metric] by [result].
Led/supervised [#] staff or contractors delivering [service]; set priorities and tracked deliverables against [standard or deadline].
interview_questions: Describe a time you advised senior leaders on a sensitive employee relations matter: what did you recommend, and what happened?
How have you managed FERS retirement or FEHB benefits casework to make sure it was accurate and compliant?
Tell us about a process improvement you led that improved customer service delivery.
How would you keep HR services running while your staff are deployed to a disaster?
watch_outs: The specialized experience in federal HR, retirement, and benefits is almost certainly missing from your background, so you would likely be rated not qualified.
The posting is open for only five days (10/26–10/30/2026).
Deployment can be extensive and come with little notice, often in austere conditions.
Schedule Policy/Career positions are at-will, with no MSPB appeal rights for adverse actions.
